back: (Actual price - standard price) × actual units sold. Positive = favourable.
(Actual units - budgeted units) × standard profit (or contribution) per unit. Positive = favourable.
Sales price variance + sales volume variance = actual margin at standard cost - budgeted margin.
Extra units also incur costs, so only the margin is extra profit. Revenue would overstate the effect.
Absorption: standard profit per unit after fixed overhead. Marginal: standard contribution per unit. The question states which.
A price cut may raise volume (adverse price, favourable volume); a price rise may lose volume. Judge the net effect.
Discounts, competition, demand, promotions, quality, price rises.
Marketing, price changes, new customers, supply shortages, seasons, competitors.
For sales, more price or more units than standard is favourable; the reverse of cost variances.
